reasoning: The aliasing is real (ctor lines 630-633 bind the same DualView as _bonus/t_bonus_1d_randomread and _bonusw/t_bonus_1d, and k_ellipsoid as _ellipsoid/_ellipsoidw), but the claimed index overlap cannot happen, so no thread ever reads a slot another thread writes. Traced how copylist_bonus is built, in CommKokkos::exchange_device (src/KOKKOS/comm_kokkos.cpp:1244-1285): k_exchange_sendlist_bonus is sorted ascending, and the backfill loop picks 'icopy' by walking down from nlocal_bonus-1 with 'if (icopy == sendlist_bonus(sendpos)) icopy--;' plus the while-loop 'while (sendpos > 0 && icopy <= sendlist_bonus(sendpos-1)) { sendpos--; icopy = sendlist_bonus(sendpos)-1; }'. That is the standard highest-surviving-index scan, so every value stored into k_exchange_copylist_bonus is a bonus slot that is NOT in exchange_sendlist_bonus. In the functor: each thread packs from _bonus(_ellipsoid[i]) = its OWN sent slot i_bonus, and writes only to _bonusw[i_bonus] (its own sent slot, distinct per atom) and _ellipsoidw[_bonus[j_bonus].ilocal] (the local atom owning a SURVIVING bonus slot, hence not a sent atom). The set written (sent bonus slots / surviving atoms) and the set read (own sent slot / surviving bonus slot j_bonus / sent atoms' ellipsoid entries) are disjoint. The scenario in the finding -- 'copylist_bonus tail entry for one is the i_bonus slot of the other' -- is exactly what that skip logic excludes. Residual nit only: binding one View both as _const_randomread (__ldg on CUDA) and writable in the same kernel is formally UB, but since no thread reads a location any thread writes, even a stale read-only cache returns the correct value here; the base AtomVecKokkos_PackExchange (atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:2198-2250) avoids the double alias by using plain writable views.

All three claims check out. (1) sort_kokkos (lines 174-190) ends with 'Sorter.sort(LMPDeviceType(), d_ellipsoid); Sorter.sort(LMPDeviceType(), d_bonus);'. The BinSort permutation is the per-atom bin permutation, but bonus is a compacted array of nlocal_bonus <= nlocal entries indexed by ellipsoid[i], so permuting it by atom index is meaningless, and nothing afterwards repairs bonus[k].ilocal (which is also invalidated by permuting the atoms themselves). (2) d_bonus is declared at atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.h:118 and grep over the .cpp shows line 187 is its only occurrence -- AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos::grow_pointers() (lines 113-151) assigns d_tag...d_ellipsoid but never d_bonus, and grow_bonus() (157-168) only calls memoryKK->grow_kokkos(k_bonus,bonus). So it is a default-constructed, zero-extent view; BinSort::sort on a view whose extent does not match the sorted range would abort, not silently misbehave. (3) The path is indeed dead today: AtomKokkos::sort() (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:345-353) computes 'int bonus_flag = (ellipsoid_flag || line_flag || tri_flag || body_flag);' and unconditionally sets sort_legacy = true for it, so sort_device() (and hence sort_kokkos) is never reached for atom_style ellipsoid/kk. reasoning: The mismatch is real but only on the remote-receive velocity path; the pack side is fine by accident, and severity is higher than 'low'. Read all four sides. (a) AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos_PackBorderBonus (ctor 452-471) and _UnpackBorderBonus (ctor 517-543) store '_buf(buf)' -- the raw 2D view, so the row stride is the DualView's own extent(1). (b) AtomVecKokkos_PackBorderVel and _UnpackBorderVel instead re-view: 'const size_t elements = atomKK->avecKK->size_border + atomKK->avecKK->size_velocity; _buf = t_double_2d_lr[_const]_um(buf.data(),maxsend,elements);' (atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:1825-1828 and 2045-2047). The non-velocity AtomVecKokkos_UnpackBorder uses the raw view like the bonus functor, so the non-vel path is consistent. (c) CommKokkos::grow_send_kokkos widens k_buf_send to size_border+size_velocity under ghost_velocity (comm_kokkos.cpp:1877-1894), but grow_recv_kokkos always allocates k_buf_recv with extent(1) = atomKK->avecKK->size_border (1905-1910). (d) CommKokkos::borders_device unpacks from k_buf_send for a self-swap and from k_buf_recv for a real neighbor (1730-1740). So: pack always writes into k_buf_send, whose extent(1) already equals size_border+size_velocity when ghost_velocity -- stride matches, no bug there; the self-swap unpack also reads k_buf_send -- matches. Only 'sendproc[iswap] != me' + ghost_velocity is broken: for ellipsoid size_border = 6+1(rmass)+8(bonus) = 15 and size_velocity = 6, so UnpackBorderVel walks the buffer at stride 21 while UnpackBorderBonus walks the same buffer at stride 15 and reads columns 13..20, i.e. flat i*15+13 instead of i*21+13. Ghost ellipsoid flag/shape/quat then come from the wrong atom. (Note Comm::size_border already includes size_velocity under ghost_velocity, src/comm.cpp:196-199, so the MPI message size and total allocation are fine -- only extent(1) is wrong.)

Alternatively (or additionally) make CommKokkos::grow_recv_kokkos allocate extent(1) = size_border + size_velocity when ghost_velocity, mirroring grow_send_kokkos, which would also remove the latent shape inconsistency between the two buffers.

Read both sides. src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:31 'static constexpr double SMALLG = 2.3e-308;' and 221-223 '// avoid overflow / if (sum_g_i < sum_numerator * static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALLG)) sum_g_i = sum_numerator * static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALLG);'. src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:400-409 makes KK_FLOAT = float under LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE and LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE (double only under the default LMP_KOKKOS_DOUBLE_DOUBLE). 2.3e-308 is far below FLT_MIN_DENORM (~1.4e-45), so static_cast<float>(SMALLG) is exactly 0.0f and the guard collapses to 'if (sum_g_i < 0.0f)', which never fires for the case it exists to catch (sum_g_i underflowed to 0). sum_g_i is then consumed at 228 'eangle = -kbt * Kokkos::log(sum_g_i);' and 230 'a = -4.0*kbt*(sum_numerator/sum_g_i)*s;' giving -inf and inf/NaN. The CPU base does the identical guard but in double (src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_gaussian.cpp:32 and 135), where sum_numerator*2.3e-308 stays a representable normal number for O(1) sum_numerator, so the guard works there. Nothing else clamps sum_g_i. Reachable: g_i = prefactor*exp(-2*dtheta^2/w^2) underflows to 0.0f once |dtheta|/w exceeds about 6.6, which is ordinary for narrow Gaussian widths. Downgraded to medium-low because it only bites the non-default single/mixed precision builds, and even in double the guard is only meaningful when sum_numerator > 0 (for sum_numerator < 0 the right-hand side is negative and the guard never fires on either side -- a pre-existing base-class weakness, not a port defect).
fix: Do the clamp in double, or floor with a type-appropriate constant: replace lines 221-223 with something like 'const KK_FLOAT smallg = std::numeric_limits<KK_FLOAT>::min(); if (sum_g_i < sum_numerator * smallg) sum_g_i = sum_numerator * smallg;' (declare smallg as a KK_FLOAT constant near SMALL rather than casting the double SMALLG). Keep the double 2.3e-308 only in the double build.
